explanation: This pole is a legal-notice detector: it fires on the stock wording of software licences, copyright notices and terms-of-use statements — 'Permission is hereby granted, free of charge', 'INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO', 'WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND', 'or (at your option) any later version', 'distributed under the License', 'All rights reserved', 'Terms of use' — with peaks of 1.2-2.9 and a sustained 0.3-0.7 across a whole licence passage (every MIT/BSD/GPL/LGPL/Apache/MPL/CC/Unlicense notice tested peaked at 0.72-2.8). The peak falls below the activity line (0.25 x max = 0.72) when the same legal vocabulary is used out of register ('seats are limited to fifty' 0.21, 'a vegetarian option' 0.00, 'charge the customer' 0.00, 'reserved a table' 0.13, 'still under warranty' 0.44), when the same permissions are reworded in ordinary language (0.14-0.36), and in obligation-style legal prose such as contracts, insurance and privacy policies (0.03-0.62), narrative, encyclopedic, news and technical prose (0.03-0.19) and source code (0.00); a leftover it does not cover is the isolated single-token spike on subword pieces of rare or foreign words ('qu' in 'roqueforti' 1.73, Greek 1.5-2.2, Russian/Arabic/Hindi 1.1-1.3).
